summary:
Radar for 2026-10-21, GLP-1 focus only. Three stories are breaking fastest.

1. Compounded tirzepatide recall: a wave of mainstream coverage (USA Today, LA Times, Fox Business, NY Post, MassLive) on Oct 20 about a Class II FDA recall of 22 compounded tirzepatide vials. Several headlines wrongly suggest Mounjaro and Zepbound themselves are affected. Coverage of FDA inspections at Chinese ingredient plants (black mold, insects) adds to it. This fits Lane B: a calm "what the FDA has actually confirmed" piece that clears up the brand confusion.
2. CagriSema in women: Novo reported a 25.0% average weight loss in women vs 3.0% on placebo at week 68. It is a post hoc analysis of REDEFINE 1, presented at The Menopause Society meeting on Oct 20. It qualifies for Lane C (first explainer) only if it ships within 48 hours. The title must say "in women" and "post hoc", and that the drug is not approved.
3. Retatrutide: Lilly's CEO statements, the Penn Reddit side-effect study, Dutch reports of illegal use and Lilly's Q3 results on Oct 29 keep it hot. Best used as the planned Lane B long-form ("Retatrutide Online: what the FDA and Lilly have confirmed"). Correction to the input feed: Lilly's six lawsuits date from August 2026, so they are background, not news.

Good Lane A (search-question) refreshers: GLP-1 and menopause (STEP UP life-stage analysis plus a cohort linking hormone therapy to more weight loss), "what to eat on GLP-1" (The Conversation, Oct 20), GLP-1 supplements vs the real medicine (Reuters, Oct 20), and why people stop semaglutide early (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19). Lower priority: orforglipron's ACHIEVE-4 heart data, semaglutide and muscle strength (handgrip meta-analysis), kidney safety from FLOW, generic semaglutide in Canada and 2027 prices, schizophrenia and alcohol research, and sleep apnea.

Rejected: an NY Post piece pushing a telehealth "GLP-1 in 48 hours for under $100" offer, and a 'technical guide' to reconstituting retatrutide 'reference vials'. Both send people toward buying unapproved or gray-market products.

Verified: the recall (Apothecary Pharma, Class II, 18 mg/mL vials, lots AP-202622 to AP-202644), the CagriSema numbers, ACHIEVE-4, the Lancet Psychiatry cohort and the menopause data. The KwikPen 'approval' in the feed is old (Jan 2026), so it isn't news.

candidates.topic: Compounded tirzepatide recall (Oct 2026): 22 lots of compounded vials recalled over sterility, Class II per FDA. Branded Mounjaro/Zepbound pens are not part of it
candidates.angle: Lane B long-form plus the 13:00 lead Short, in the 'What's Actually Confirmed?' series. Several headlines ('Mounjaro, Zepbound ingredient risk raised') imply the brand-name pens are affected. Calmly explain what the FDA notice actually covers: compounded tirzepatide 18 mg/mL multi-dose vials; voluntary recall started Sept 24; FDA classed it Class II on Oct 8. Explain what Class II means and why sterility matters for injectables. Add the FDA's inspection findings at Chinese ingredient plants (mould, insects; firms put on import alert). End by telling viewers to ask their pharmacist or prescriber whether their product is affected and about approved options. Say 'a compounding pharmacy' rather than promoting any company. No buying guidance. Title idea: 'Tirzepatide Recall: What the FDA Has Confirmed (Oct 2026)'
candidates.why_now: National outlets covered it within the last 24 h (USA Today, LA Times, Fox Business, NY Post, MassLive, Tennessean), and headline confusion is driving 'is my Mounjaro recalled' searches. It matches our strongest Short lane (gray-market 'what's confirmed', median 108) and Lane B long-form. The FDA's inspection findings on Chinese ingredient makers (LA Times, Oct 19) make it a stronger story.

evidence.signal: Recall of 22 vials, Oct 8 FDA notice, Class II, voluntary recall from Sept 24, Dec 2025 FDA warning letter
Lots AP-202622 to AP-202644, 18 mg/mL 4 mL multi-dose vials, beyond-use dates Oct 7 to Nov 26
'Mounjaro, Zepbound ingredient risk raised to second-highest level' headline shows the brand confusion

evidence.source: NewsBytes summary of FDA inspection findings
evidence.signal: Black mold, insects at Chinese semaglutide/tirzepatide ingredient plants; firms put on import alert

candidates.topic: CagriSema in women: 25.0% average weight loss vs 3.0% on placebo at week 68 (REDEFINE 1 post hoc analysis, Menopause Society meeting, Oct 20, 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane C 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded' long-form, only if it ships by Oct 22. Title starts with the new name: 'CagriSema in Women: What the New 25% Result Means'. Explain what CagriSema is (cagrilintide plus semaglutide). Cover the post hoc result in women and the split by menopause stage: 26.7% premenopausal, 24.8% perimenopausal, 23.1% postmenopausal (1,902 women). Note that the full trial averaged 22.7%. Explain what 'post hoc' means. Status: not approved; Novo expects a US decision in Q4 2026; side effects mainly gastrointestinal. Do not call it head-to-head with tirzepatide. Funnel Short at 20:00 the next day.
candidates.why_now: First reported Oct 20 by Reuters, CNBC and Quartz. Few health creators have explained it yet, and Lane C rewards being first within 48 h (EloraTZP: 442). The menopause angle reaches our 40–65 female audience.

evidence.signal: Novo's next-generation obesity drug shows 25% weight loss in women in late-stage analysis (Oct 20, 2026)
25.0% vs 3.0% placebo at week 68; menopause-stage split; waist −20.5 cm vs −4.7 cm
Reuters copy: post hoc REDEFINE 1, Menopause Society 2026 Annual Meeting
New meta-analysis: CagriSema vs semaglutide 2.4 mg

candidates.topic: Retatrutide online: what the FDA and Lilly have confirmed (Oct 2026), ahead of Lilly's Q3 results on Oct 29
candidates.angle: The planned Lane B long-form ('Retatrutide Online: What the FDA and Lilly Have Confirmed'). Credit and date every line: not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026. Lilly's CMO said black-market product 'is not a medicine' (lawsuits filed Aug 2026). Penn's Reddit AI study (preprint): users self-reported increased appetite, fatigue and insomnia more often than the trials did. Netherlands authorities report rising illegal use. Trial results so far. Never name sellers; point to a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials.
candidates.why_now: Several sources in the last 48 h: the Penn study (SciTechDaily, MedPage), NL Times on illegal use, Lilly CEO comments on retatrutide as its next growth driver, and Medscape on whether retatrutide could break a GLP-1 plateau. Earnings on Oct 29 will bring another spike. Retatrutide in a 'what's confirmed' frame is our best Short topic (184, 116).

evidence.signal: Lilly filed six lawsuits against companies allegedly selling retatrutide (date it as Aug 2026, not new)
CMO Hyman: black-market product 'is not a medicine'
Retatrutide FDA approval status page (check it on the day of publishing)

candidates.topic: GLP-1 and menopause: does weight loss differ before, during and after menopause? (STEP UP life-stage analysis, plus a cohort linking hormone therapy to more semaglutide weight loss)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 'GLP-1 and Menopause: What the Research Shows'. STEP UP post hoc (semaglutide 7.2 mg, adults with obesity without diabetes, 72 weeks): about 22.6% premenopausal vs about 19.7–19.8% peri- and postmenopausal. Observational cohort: women on semaglutide plus hormone therapy lost 16% vs 12% without it at 12 months ('linked to', not 'causes'). Tie in the new CagriSema women's data as a re-hook. Never suggest starting hormone therapy for weight loss; talk to your doctor. Not a repeat of a recent Short.
candidates.why_now: Everyday Health and Bioengineer covered the HRT and semaglutide cohort on Oct 20, MedPage ran 'GLP-1 in Menopause', and the Menopause Society meeting is underway. Real search demand from women 40–60 in high-CPM markets.

evidence.signal: STEP UP post hoc: 22.6% premenopausal, 19.7% perimenopausal, 19.8% postmenopausal; HRT 16% vs 12%
Earlier finding: hormone therapy may boost weight loss for postmenopausal women on semaglutide
CagriSema results by menopause stage, a fresh hook

candidates.topic: Is my GLP-1 real? Branded vs compounded vs counterfeit: what the FDA and MHRA say to check (Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane B evergreen companion to the recall video: 'Counterfeit Semaglutide and Tirzepatide Pens: What the FDA Says to Check'. Cover FDA crackdown statements, the MHRA's seizure of 12,000+ counterfeit pens (Oct 14), the photo-review study (26% on compounded products, 65% of those thought they were branded), and the Brazil black market (Bloomberg). Packaging checks from regulator pages only; ask your pharmacist. Never name sellers.
keywords: fake Ozempic pen how to tell
candidates.why_now: McClatchy ran 'Is my GLP-1 safe? What to know about FDA's crackdown on copycat drugs' on Oct 20. The recall wave, Bloomberg's Brazil piece and last week's MHRA raid all point the same way. Lane B is our strongest lane.

evidence.signal: 'Is my GLP-1 safe? What to know about FDA's crackdown on copycat drugs' (Oct 20)
Background on compounded GLP-1 production
Regulatory basis for blocked ingredient imports

candidates.topic: GLP-1 'supplements' vs the real medicine: doctors and regulators raise flags (Reuters, Oct 20)
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'GLP-1 Supplements: Do They Work Like Ozempic?' Explain the difference between a prescription GLP-1 drug and products marketed as 'GLP-1 support'. FDA warnings about tainted weight-loss supplements. Then the positive part: protein, fibre and eating vegetables and protein first can modestly raise your own GLP-1, without claiming they replace the medicine. Mention that 'companion products' are a growing market (Nutrition Insight).
candidates.why_now: Reuters story on Oct 20, plus Nutrition Insight on companion products. The topic was in our previous snapshot at 64 and is accelerating. High search volume, and it supports the 'natural ways to support your GLP-1' pillar.

evidence.signal: 'As weight-loss drug users turn to dietary supplements, doctors and regulators raise flags' (Oct 20)
Background: 'natural' diet pills found tainted with sibutramine

candidates.topic: What to eat on tirzepatide or semaglutide: protein, fibre and easier meals (The Conversation, Oct 20, plus a new rapid review on protein and resistance training)
candidates.angle: Lane A 'Life on GLP-1' long-form: 'What to Eat on Tirzepatide: Protein, Fibre and Easier Meals'. Protein at each meal (check first if you have kidney disease), fibre, fluids (unless told to limit them), smaller meals, eating slower, foods that make nausea easier. Muscle outcome: about how much of the weight lost is lean mass in the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy. Use 'recommended' wording for guideline habits.
candidates.why_now: The Conversation explainer published Oct 20. The Nutrients rapid review (Oct 2) gives fresh evidence. Steady high-volume search phrase that fits the playbook's Lane A examples exactly.

evidence.signal: 'Started a GLP-1 drug like Ozempic or Mounjaro? Here's what you need to know about nutrition' (Oct 20)
Protein intake and resistance training across clinical populations: rapid review

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide make you weaker? New meta-analysis of handgrip strength on semaglutide (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Muscle outcome Short ('Semaglutide and muscle: weaker or not?'), then a Lane A long-form, 'Does Semaglutide Cause Muscle Loss? Mass vs Strength'. Separate lean mass from muscle function. Use the new meta-analysis only after reading its abstract for the direction and size of the effect. SEMALEAN (handgrip +4.5 kg at 12 months, observational) is background. Strength training (start gently) and protein help.
candidates.why_now: Meta-analysis published Oct 19 with no news coverage yet. Muscle question Shorts are proven (100, 131 views). Creators haven't picked it up.

evidence.signal: Changes in muscle strength following semaglutide: systematic review and meta-analysis of handgrip strength (Oct 19)
Handgrip +4.5 kg at 12 months; sarcopenic obesity 49% to 33%

candidates.topic: Why do so many people stop semaglutide early? Real-world US data on how starting habits relate to stopping early and staying on for 1 year (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'Why Do People Stop Ozempic or Wegovy? What the Data Shows'. Report the findings on early stopping and persistence, then what helps: tackling side effects early, protein, eating slowly, talking to the prescriber. Never advise stopping or titration. Re-hook: what happens after stopping (SURMOUNT-4 / STEP 4), linking to the 'stopping' series.
keywords: how long do people stay on Ozempic
candidates.why_now: New paper published Oct 19, plus AJMC (Oct 20) on patients being open to lower-cost maintenance. Pairs with our recurring 'after stopping' snapshot topic (seen 6×, around 66).

evidence.signal: Real-world semaglutide initiation behaviours: impact on early discontinuation and 1-year persistence

candidates.topic: UK Mounjaro price rise: what happened to more than 1 million self-paying UK adults' treatment patterns and weight (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 14)
candidates.angle: Single-drug Short and a UK-focused Lane A long-form: 'Mounjaro Price Rise UK: What Happened Next'. Describe the observed patterns (switching, gaps, weight outcomes) strictly as reported. Never advise switching, stopping or dose-stretching. Talk to your prescriber about options.
candidates.why_now: A very large real-world UK dataset that UK news hasn't picked up yet. UK is a high-CPM audience, and the title names 'tirzepatide/Mounjaro' (our biggest Short lever).

evidence.signal: Treatment patterns and weight outcomes before and after a tirzepatide price increase in >1M self-paying UK adults

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) and the heart: ACHIEVE-4 non-inferior to insulin glargine for major heart events in type 2 diabetes; CHMP backed it in the EU (Oct 16)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 'Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill: Heart Safety and What's Confirmed'. Primary result: MACE-4 non-inferior vs insulin glargine (16% lower, relative). The cardiovascular-death and all-cause-death figures were pre-planned secondary analyses and must be labelled as such. Population: type 2 diabetes with heart risk, more than 2,700 people. EU: CHMP recommended, Commission decision pending. Orforglipron-only Shorts underperform, so keep this long-form only.
candidates.why_now: Clinical Trial Vanguard analysis on Oct 19, the CHMP opinion on Oct 16 (snapshot momentum 82–84), and the qualitative orforglipron study in Patient (Oct 16). An EU decision could arrive soon and would qualify as Lane C.

evidence.signal: ACHIEVE-4: MACE-4 non-inferior vs insulin glargine; Lancet publication; EASD 2026

candidates.topic: Will Ozempic get cheaper? Generic semaglutide in Canada, plus Novo's US list-price cuts from January 2027
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'Will Ozempic Get Cheaper? Generics and 2027 Prices Explained'. Health Canada's review of generic semaglutide applications (IQVIA analysis, Oct 20; check the current approval and launch status on the day) and Novo's announced US list-price cuts. Date everything. Say 'don't switch or stop your current medicines on your own', and generics are not the same as compounded products.
candidates.why_now: IQVIA report on Oct 20, Novo's Wegovy price cut in China, and recurring snapshot topics (seen 4×, around 60). Strong search demand from Canada and the US.

Add the Diabetic Medicine real-world tirzepatide CKD study (observational). Tell viewers with kidney disease to check protein and fluid targets with their care team.
